newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK May PMI survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK May PMI survey.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the May UK Purchasing Managers' Survey, which showed the 12th consecutive monthly expansion in manufacturing activity.
The seasonally adjusted PMI index rose to 54.6, the highest level since April 1995, from 53.6 in April.
"The figures show a very strong manufacturing sector...The case is building for a 25-basis point interest rate hike by the end of this week."

"Despite the apparent lack of price pressures, the report is consistent with a continued expansion in the manufacturing sector. The odds remain just about in favour of a monetary tightening this week. The deceleration of M0 over recent months is at odds with buoyant consumer spending and therefore rather curious."

"The UK data are mixed and on balance should not be seen as strong enough to prompt a hike in rates this week. The CIPS survey is consistent with other surveys in painting an increasingly robust picture of manufacturing. Moreover, despite all the rhetoric, the exports component held up remarkably well. This should offer stg some support. The other data were less inspiring...Net, data good enough to reinforce the impression of an economy that is doing well, and with perhaps a better balance to growth than previously seemed likely."
